sites.name: a currently paid bound migration keeps Stage 2 access independently of the old cutoff
sites.rationale: An already bound paid migration bypasses the old cohort cutoff in both narrow and full loaders; ordinary post-cutoff readiness cannot detect loss of the immutable migration exception.

sites.name: verified normal paid pre-cutoff sources enter the journey only while migration is enabled
sites.rationale: Current normal-paid one-time/launch sources require the migration-enabled exception before the cutoff. This contrasts ordinary paid authority with a bound migration and preserves both disabled and enabled outcomes.

sites.name: Stage 2 access keeps the app rollout gate and stops before later-stage authority reads
sites.rationale: The app exclusion must occur before entitlement and the admitted Stage-2 read must avoid refined, draft, Stage-3 and Stage-4 dependencies. Monotonic counters make forbidden reads observable; C4 adds the timing receipt to this existing success.

sites.name: Stage 2 access remains fail-closed for incomplete owner source facts and throws on reads
sites.rationale: Independent denied states include rollout off, paid_pending/none/revoked, old cohort, Stage-2 flag off, absent artifact/initial version, and an authoritative thrown read. Happy-path union cannot preserve these gates.

sites.name: internal app rollout excludes non-internal users before plan data is read
sites.rationale: Full-loader internal rollout rejection must precede entitlement, observed with a monotonic count; narrow-loader exclusion does not establish full-route behavior.

sites.name: internal app rollout admits the internal owner to the regular journey
sites.rationale: The internal owner can pass the internal rollout gate. The external rejection and all-users rollout fixtures do not exercise the positive internal predicate.

sites.name: loader derives the frontier only from owner-scoped entitlement, source, plan and current authority facts
sites.rationale: C3: identical deps() authority facts and user-1 as timing keeper528; transfer frontier=stage4 and allowed.stage3/stage4=true to its existing returned access.

candidate.name: loader derives the frontier only from owner-scoped entitlement, source, plan and current authority facts
candidate.keeper: full journey access reports non-identifying Stage 3 sub-phase timings in dependency order

sites.name: journey access accepts a current Stage 3 draft with a valid product-load overlay
sites.rationale: A resolved extra product-load category has its own overlay authority; accepting a base-only completed draft cannot catch rejecting the valid overlay.

sites.name: journey access accepts a product-load upgrade of an existing base category
sites.rationale: The overlay upgrades an existing base deep-cleansing category instead of adding a category; append-overlay acceptance does not establish this replacement authority branch.

sites.name: journey access still rejects a semantically stale product-load overlay
sites.rationale: An altered current-product-load profile invalidates the old overlay semantically. Shape-valid authority acceptance must not admit this stale interpretation.

sites.name: full journey access reports non-identifying Stage 3 sub-phase timings in dependency order
sites.rationale: Real loader clocks three reached phases with literal names/outcomes/durations and excludes owner IDs from telemetry; C3 adds exact access outputs at the same existing call.

sites.name: full journey access stops access timing after an early entitlement denial
sites.rationale: Early paid_pending denial emits only the reached entitlement phase and stops the artifact path. Full successful timing cannot catch continuation after denial.

sites.name: full journey access reports the reached sub-phase when a dependency throws
sites.rationale: An artifact failure emits the error phase with its duration and rejects with the original diagnostic. A normal timing list does not establish error delivery.

sites.name: the narrow Stage 2 access read never emits Stage 3 access timing
sites.rationale: C4: narrow owner accepts the same active/artifact/initial-plan facts as296; add reporter and exact empty timing receipt to that existing success, preserving all zero later-read counters.

candidate.name: the narrow Stage 2 access read never emits Stage 3 access timing
candidate.keeper: Stage 2 access keeps the app rollout gate and stops before later-stage authority reads

sites.name: loader starts independent current refined-need and product-draft reads together
sites.rationale: A held refined-need promise must not delay starting the independent product-draft read. Final access equality does not establish parallel start.

sites.name: loader starts independent prepared-artifact and plan reads together
sites.rationale: A held artifact promise must not delay starting the plan read; this is a different prefix-stage concurrency edge from refined/draft.

sites.name: loader keeps paid-pending buyers on the compact wait route and throws on authoritative read failure
sites.rationale: Paid-pending recovery is identical with or without artifact lead; an active-source plan-read failure rejects with its diagnostic. The timing-denial fixture alone does not contain this input/error union.

sites.name: full journey keeps an active enrollment without an attached artifact lead on legacy routing
sites.rationale: Active enrollment without artifact lead retains legacy routing rather than promoting to personal_plan_start. The entitlement is active, unlike paid_pending denial.

sites.name: a valid refined source admits Stage 3 before a draft exists and while its current draft is active
sites.rationale: Absent and active current drafts admit Stage3 but not a completed proposal; the default completed-draft fixture does not establish both non-completed branches.

sites.name: an accepted Routine keeps Stage 4/5 reachable while a malformed successor resumes at the Stage 2 bridge
sites.rationale: F title only: actual assertions preserve accepted Routine Stage4/5 after malformed successor and expect routine_redirect at plan-start, not the Stage2-bridge behavior named in the title. Keep all current assertions.

sites.name: an accepted active Routine retains Stage 3 when its current successor authority is valid
sites.rationale: Accepted Routine plus valid current successor retains Stage3 too; degraded-successor recovery alone would permit accidentally denying all successor editing.

sites.name: the Routine page reads and renders an accepted Routine when only its successor Stage 3 access is degraded
sites.rationale: F title only: this calls the real Routine page resolver with a supplied readView and checks its returned view; it does not render React. Narrow the render claim, retain degraded-successor resolver contract.

sites.name: a pending proposal remains fail-closed when its successor source is unavailable
sites.rationale: Pending proposal without accepted immutable Routine must throw on missing current refined source; the accepted-Routine recovery exception cannot leak into proposals.

sites.name: Supabase draft selection ignores stale rows while retaining a current row, and treats stale-only as absent
sites.rationale: F private query ordering only: .at(-1) requires status filter to be last although fake and real conjunctive filters are order-independent. Keep current-row products/roles/overlay, stale-only null and literal neq:stale membership; replace last-position receipt with membership in a later zero-quota repair.

sites.name: Supabase loader keeps every journey fact owner and aggregate scoped
sites.rationale: Actual Supabase adapter calls are captured for every owner and aggregate selector. The deps() success fixtures manufacture loaded values and cannot establish these query predicates/projections.

sites.name: partner access retains its routing exemption when the account also has a trial
sites.rationale: A partner also holding a trial retains partner routing exemption; source-precedence behavior is not the trial-only or partner-only branch.

sites.name: `unpaid ${provider} trial resolves its exact quiz without paid attribution`
sites.rationale: One AST declaration loops Stripe and PayPal trial projections. Exact unpaid trial source, quiz ownership and paidAt=null discriminate real trial provenance from paid launch attribution; keep both existing runtime cases.

sites.name: trial source rejects mismatched enrollment, malformed payload and changed lead ownership
sites.rationale: Mismatched enrollment ID, malformed source payload and changed lead owner deny trial resolution. A successful RPC result does not establish binding validation.

sites.name: revoked and expired trial projections never resolve a plan source
sites.rationale: Revoked and expired trial projections must not yield a source, even with matching enrollment data; these are live-access predicates before source selection.

sites.name: trial read failures remain errors rather than an absent source
sites.rationale: Trial resolver DB failures throw instead of returning absence. An invalid source row returning none does not preserve error semantics.

sites.name: trial legacy eligibility cannot inherit the historical-paid migration bypass
sites.rationale: A legacy trial cannot borrow the historical-paid migration bypass. Both trial provenance and old lead date are operative; paid migration fixtures cannot own this negative.

sites.name: trial routing recognizes ready and pending plans while retaining ordinary cohort gates
sites.rationale: Trial ready/pending frontier projection preserves cohort gates, including no historical paid bypass. The enrollment-only output does not establish routing.

sites.name: a current Personal Plan membership resolves through its exact provider purchase and quiz lead
sites.rationale: C5: keeper394 selects the identical subscription/session/lead/time after sorting and skipping an unrelated standard subscription. Transfer all seven enrollment fields and all three exact correlation predicates.

candidate.name: a current Personal Plan membership resolves through its exact provider purchase and quiz lead
candidate.keeper: the launch membership is selected even when a standard subscription sorts ahead of it

sites.name: Stripe launch memberships use the checkout session reference persisted at activation
sites.rationale: Stripe uses checkout_session_id while PayPal uses provider_subscription_id; retaining PayPal happy path cannot catch selecting sub_personal_plan instead of cs_personal_plan.

sites.name: the launch membership is selected even when a standard subscription sorts ahead of it
sites.rationale: Actual billing selection skips a longer-lived standard subscription and resolves the same exact launch row as324. Retain selection input and add complete donor result/query union.

sites.name: standard subscriptions and membership purchases without exact Personal Plan attribution fail closed
sites.rationale: Standard catalog, missing session attribution and a legacy quiz source without an enabled legacy cutover return the full empty enrollment. Full positive result does not prove these three negative admission paths.

sites.name: an unapplied field-test relation preserves ordinary non-Personal-Plan enrollment
sites.rationale: Missing field-test relation is an allowed pre-migration absence path; unrelated database failures are separately errors.

sites.name: a stale PostgREST partner relationship hint preserves ordinary enrollment
sites.rationale: Specific stale PostgREST partner relationship hint is tolerated as unavailable optional relation; it is not the generic missing-table code.

sites.name: an active partner grant admits the exact legacy quiz indefinitely without cohort gates
sites.rationale: Live partner grant linked to exact invitation grants legacy access indefinitely despite ordinary cutoff/app gates, with owner/revocation query receipt.

sites.name: a claimed partner invitation without a lead binding or activation never grants access
sites.rationale: C6: keeper623 has the same null lead AND null activation with valid matching current partner grant; opaque IDs differ only by consistent equality. Both return identical seven-field empty object; keeper additionally excludes revoked tester fallback.

candidate.name: a claimed partner invitation without a lead binding or activation never grants access
candidate.keeper: a claimed partner's revoked tester enrollments never resurrect the old tester lead

sites.name: a claimed partner's revoked tester enrollments never resurrect the old tester lead
sites.rationale: Unbound claimed partner must not resurrect either revoked personal-plan or regular tester source. Both actual status queries exclude the extra rows; retains complete C6 denial union.

sites.name: a post-cutoff owned legacy lead is eligible only behind the independent cutover
sites.rationale: Post-cutoff owner legacy source is controlled by the independent legacy cutover, including disabled branch; personal_plan lead bypass does not exercise legacy policy.

sites.name: historical paid legacy enrollment and frontier agree when migration replaces the old cutover
sites.rationale: Historical paid legacy enrollment and frontier must agree under migration-enabled replacement of old cutover; retained normal post-cutoff source does not establish this exception.

sites.name: historical legacy eligibility still requires owner, valid date, app rollout and live payment
sites.rationale: Migration exception still requires exact owner, parseable date, rollout and current paid source. Blanket migration allowance would escape the earlier positive cases.

sites.name: a legacy moderator enrollment uses its persisted source discriminator
sites.rationale: Persisted moderator quiz_source_kind=legacy selects legacy source while its actual lead may be represented through field-test storage; cannot infer solely from table name.

sites.name: an unknown moderator enrollment source discriminator fails closed
sites.rationale: Unknown persisted moderator source discriminator denies admission. Positive legacy/current discriminators do not establish fail-closed unknown behavior.

sites.name: field-test enrollment reads still fail closed on unrelated database errors
sites.rationale: Unrelated DB errors remain errors instead of tolerated missing relation; preserve diagnostic distinction.

sites.name: an existing paid migration keeps its immutable source even when another launch purchase exists
sites.rationale: Ready immutable migration authority wins over a newer launch purchase and keeps bound source identity; launch-selection keeper assumes no migration.

sites.name: an unavailable migration authority never substitutes another purchase as the Plan source
sites.rationale: Unavailable migration authority throws and cannot silently substitute a live purchase; successful authority precedence cannot detect fallback after errors.

sites.name: recording a module banner dismissal and reading it back reports that module dismissed
sites.rationale: D1: exact same writer args, read args and products=true assertion already occur in119 before its additional habits=false assertion. No transfer or new input.

candidate.name: recording a module banner dismissal and reading it back reports that module dismissed
candidate.keeper: dismissing one module leaves the other module's banner un-dismissed (per-module independence, i.e. the reappear-once mechanism)

sites.name: dismissing one module leaves the other module's banner un-dismissed (per-module independence, i.e. the reappear-once mechanism)
sites.rationale: Write/read products dismissal plus independent habits=false proves module separation and exactly contains D1.

sites.name: dismissing the same module twice is idempotent: exactly one stored row, still dismissed
sites.rationale: F mock-owned idempotence: fake Map always uses user|kind|subject and ignores upsert options; wrong conflict target can remain green here. Retain two-write case, report lack of actual transport-option/DB proof; no deletion credit.

sites.name: dismissals are scoped per user: another user's dismissal never hides this user's banner
sites.rationale: Real selectSubjects query excludes a different user before membership. Add exact empty set from C1 so unrelated invented dismissed subjects cannot pass.

sites.name: a user with no dismissals reads as no modules dismissed
sites.rationale: C1: actual load owner receives data=[] both here and after148 foreign-owner filtering. Add literal full empty set to148; no new read or row.

candidate.name: a user with no dismissals reads as no modules dismissed
candidate.keeper: dismissals are scoped per user: another user's dismissal never hides this user's banner

sites.name: module dismissal read degrades to 'no dismissals' (banner visible) when the table/columns are absent
sites.rationale: Returned database error degrades banner visibility to both modules not dismissed; synchronous exceptions exercise a separate catch path.

sites.name: module dismissal read degrades to 'no dismissals' when the client throws synchronously
sites.rationale: Synchronous from() throw reaches outer catch and returns exact empty dismissal state, unlike a returned query error.

sites.name: a stored subject outside the known module set is ignored rather than crashing the read
sites.rationale: Unknown stored subject is filtered from real loaded rows; an empty database cannot catch omission of the known-module whitelist.

sites.name: recording a module banner dismissal surfaces a write error to the caller
sites.rationale: Write error propagates to API caller instead of being swallowed like reads; read degradation does not establish write semantics.

sites.name: recording a nav surface visit and reading it back reports that surface visited
sites.rationale: C2: keeper258 performs identical profile writer/read under same user/time plus one other-kind row. Transfer available=true and profile/application membership booleans to the existing visited state.

candidate.name: recording a nav surface visit and reading it back reports that surface visited
candidate.keeper: nav-visited state is independent per module-banner state: the two kinds never leak into each other

sites.name: a user with no visits reads as available with nothing visited (every non-routine tab dots)
sites.rationale: Successful zero rows is available=true and means unvisited dots; unavailable empty rows must remain distinct. Both chat/profile positive dots retained.

sites.name: routine is never dotted, visited or not
sites.rationale: Routine is never dotted before or after its own persisted visit. Other surfaces use membership and cannot establish this special exclusion.

sites.name: a visited surface no longer shows the unvisited dot
sites.rationale: Persisted chat visit removes chat dot while profile stays unvisited. The proposed profile keeper cannot catch a defect dropping chat from the stored allowed-surface set; retain.

sites.name: visiting the same nav surface twice is idempotent: exactly one stored row
sites.rationale: F mock-owned idempotence: Map imposes the PK independently of actual upsert conflict options. Keep repeated application visit but do not call this Postgres uniqueness proof.

sites.name: nav-visited state is independent per module-banner state: the two kinds never leak into each other
sites.rationale: Same profile visit/read as C2 with a products dismissal also present; literal sets protect actual kind separation. Add donor availability and helper-membership assertions.

sites.name: nav-visited read degrades to unavailable — no dots anywhere, NOT a dot on every tab — when the table is absent
sites.rationale: Returned table error makes available=false and suppresses chat/profile dots, contrasting successful empty rows. Preserve both signal and downstream decision.

sites.name: nav-visited read degrades to unavailable when the client throws synchronously
sites.rationale: Synchronous query-construction failure must also suppress dots; returned error keeper does not exercise this exception path.

sites.name: recording a nav surface visit surfaces a write error to the caller
sites.rationale: Nav write error propagates to deferred caller for its own recovery; banner writer error does not establish nav wrapper wiring.

sites.name: quiz transition direction follows the navigation action, not screen order
sites.rationale: Back/advance action controls animation independent of numeric screen order; history stack tests do not observe animation direction.

sites.name: approved flow inserts the analysis bridge, midpoint, admission ladder, and daily commitment
sites.rationale: Literal successful next screens cover positive/no-concern branch plus structural phase transitions. Current optional scalp conflict is a different predicate and phase.

sites.name: recurrence keeps ordinary history-stack Back semantics after moving beside concerns
sites.rationale: Appending same last screen is idempotent while recurrence extends history; next-screen mapping cannot detect broken Back stack ownership.

sites.name: five stable checkpoint sections cover every semantic phase
sites.rationale: Section labels drive restored progress/animation, with recurrence assigned goals_and_context and emotional relevance analysis. Routing sequence equality does not establish section membership.

sites.name: scalp concerns use one optional multi-select screen without a medical warning branch
sites.rationale: Optional scalp screen routes no trade-off to practical cost and fine+moisture to conflict. Both empty and dryness-only cannot activate conflict without a supported pair.

sites.name: the later scalp tail still reaches a conflict prompt after recurrence moved earlier
sites.rationale: Oily scalp+dry lengths selects the other conflict predicate and conflict advances to practical cost. Fine/moisture test does not establish oily branch or outgoing conflict transition.

sites.name: browser draft trims malformed current concern notes without resetting v4 drafts
sites.rationale: Save/load trims and caps malformed note at50 while keeping draft version4. Server reject-long schema differs intentionally from tolerant browser restoration.

sites.name: conflicting-needs prompt is shown only for a supported trade-off
sites.rationale: Exact prompt ID/copy for oily, fine, textured and treated trade-offs plus null unsupported input. Screen routing only checks truthiness and cannot establish these emitted messages.

sites.name: goals retain all eight selected domains without a cap
sites.rationale: All eight selected goals survive browser roundtrip; server payload acceptance alone does not establish localStorage projection.

sites.name: draft preserves an explicit no-concerns answer across reloads
sites.rationale: Explicit empty concerns survives as [] rather than omitted undefined, which controls whether the question is answered; malformed/missing concerns are not equivalent.

sites.name: prepared-plan answer keys survive the draft's canonical field ordering
sites.rationale: F correlated key oracle: both expected and actual call getPersonalPlanQuizAnswersKey, so constant-key fault passes despite active prepare-cache use. Keep ordering input and add independent fixed canonical object/string receipt in later zero-quota repair; no new input required.

sites.name: stale elasticity opt-outs return the user to the required test
sites.rationale: Retired unknown elasticity rewinds screen/history to required test and removes obsolete answer. Generic malformed JSON null cannot detect this compatibility route.

sites.name: v4 drafts preserve exact concern recurrence and reject the retired v3 schema
sites.rationale: Exact selected recurrence survives; dangling recurrence is discarded; retired v3 draft is refused. Browser current-version and server persistence contracts are independent.

sites.name: draft excludes lead PII and all conversion-only answers
sites.rationale: Raw stored bytes exclude PII and ephemeral conversion fields, then durable answers reload correctly. Object-only projection cannot prove storage privacy.

sites.name: draft ignores removed rough-flow fields and malformed storage
sites.rationale: Removed rough-flow fields disappear and invalid JSON restores null. Active durable fields positive case cannot establish former-schema rejection.

sites.name: draft persistence tolerates restricted storage
sites.rationale: Quota and blocked removal exceptions are tolerated; ordinary MemoryStorage cannot exercise browser storage failure.

sites.name: profile summary stays positive and derives four useful rows from durable answers
sites.rationale: Wavy/fine/medium moisture+dry scalp flexible profile emits four positive German rows and excludes medical framing. Other profile comparisons do not preserve these particular labels.

sites.name: materially different profiles produce recognizably different positive receipts
sites.rationale: Straight volume, curly treated strengthening/shape, and coily irritated contexts produce distinct public receipts and exact composite phrases; current helper consumes all relevant inputs.

sites.name: the ten dimensions use only the approved primary, observation and support weights
sites.rationale: All ten literal evidence scores over deliberately crowded primary/observation/support input preserve numeric weights/caps, not merely three displayed IDs.

sites.name: hair-loss dimension is pinned second for assessment tie-breaks
sites.rationale: Array order is actually used as final assessment sort tie-break. Current hair-loss copy fixture has moisture goal boost, so it does not prove hair-loss-before-moisture on tied priority; no same-input public keeper preserves this literal ordering.

sites.name: support and goals cannot activate a dimension or worsen its visible band
sites.rationale: Support/goal-only facts cannot activate/worsen dimensions; literal segment conversion boundaries are preserved too. Active high-evidence rows cannot establish absence semantics.

sites.name: goals and exact-concern recurrence affect ordering only
sites.rationale: Goals and exact selected recurrence reorder priorities while evidence scores remain unchanged; numeric score fixture cannot detect priorities accidentally affecting visible band.

sites.name: surface and shine are display siblings while breakage and split ends stay independent
sites.rationale: Surface/shine are display siblings while breakage/split stay independently selectable. Generic unique cardinality does not establish specific sibling policy.

sites.name: Haarschäden and Frizz stay independent assessment signals
sites.rationale: Generic hair damage and frizz are independent signals rather than aliases; explicit evidence, selected dimensions and copy must not collapse them.

sites.name: generic damage honors its exact recurrence only as an ordering tie-break
sites.rationale: Only recurrence bound to hair_damage changes its ordering; unrelated concern recurrence cannot promote it. Generic recurrence keeper has other IDs.

sites.name: hair-loss assessment row uses the reviewed cautious two-sentence copy
sites.rationale: Literal medically cautious two-sentence hair-loss copy is an independently reviewed visible claim, not replaceable by word-count or selected-ID checks.

sites.name: explicit Haarschäden copy takes precedence over a stays-stretched observation
sites.rationale: Explicit hair_damage copy outranks stays-stretched observation; observation-only Stability row must remain a separate branch.

sites.name: legacy factual answers adapt to the shared diagnosis without invented context
sites.rationale: Actual legacy factual adapter maps fields without synthesizing unasked context, then assessment remains valid. Modern answers bypass adapter and cannot preserve migration vocabulary.

sites.name: a stretch observation cannot place Haarbruch beside explicitly selected Spliss
sites.rationale: Explicit Spliss suppresses a second observation-only Haarbruch row; ordinary sibling surface/shine is a separate exclusion.

sites.name: a stays-stretched observation guarantees a neutral Stability row without claiming Haarbruch
sites.rationale: Stays-stretched observation yields neutral Stability title/segment/literal explanation without claiming explicit breakage. Generic damage fixture selects explicit concern branch.

sites.name: scalp irritation is retained regardless of concern order
sites.rationale: Irritation remains in evidence and public tolerance copy under both scalp-concern orders. A single fixed first concern cannot catch accidental order dependence.

sites.name: positive fill uses only explicit neutral observations and still respects siblings
sites.rationale: Positive fill requires explicit neutral facts and respects shine/surface siblings; selected IDs and cautious flexible copy are fixed independently.

sites.name: an active dimension is not selected again as positive fill
sites.rationale: An active frizz dimension is not repeated as positive smooth-surface fill; other sibling input does not have same active/neutral overlap.

sites.name: crowded evidence ownership omits lower-priority clauses instead of breaking the copy contract
sites.rationale: Three existing crowded inputs check external word/sentence/answer-highlight limits. Exhaustive376 chooses a single goal by concern-mask modulus and does not contain the complete ranking/ownership input union (notably multi-goal scenario). Keep whole declaration.

sites.name: every selectable concern and observation composition stays inside the public copy contract
sites.rationale: Existing exhaustive compositions cover all concern subsets and observation/treatment/length combinations for a prescribed goal selection, requiring three unique dimensions and nonthrowing public rows. Named examples do not contain this existing generated domain.

sites.name: all reviewed row families keep public copy within two sentences and 28 words
sites.rationale: Eleven reviewed families independently check public word/sentence bounds and answer markup; exhaustive376 relies on owner-internal validator for bounds and does not assert answer text excludes angle brackets.
